texts.preamble: In Re: Prosenjit Ghosh vs The State Of West Bengal on 12 October, 2017 Author: Harish Tandon
texts.arguments: It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the prosecution has launched the criminal proceeding under sections 272/273/420/120B of the Indian Penal Code when In Re: Prosenjit Ghosh vs The State Of West Bengal on 12 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74694269/ 1 there is a Special Act being the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It is further submitted that there is a special procedure provided for investigation in relation to an offence committed under the Special Act and in view of the judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Jeewan Kumar Raut & Another - Vs- Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in (2009) 7 Supreme Court Cases 526, the charging sections under the Indian Penal Code is impliedly overruled and/or superseded by the provisions 2 of the Special Act. It would be apt to quote the observation recorded in paragraph 26 of the said judgment, which runs thus : "It is a well-settled principle of law that if a special statute lays down procedures, the ones laid down under the general statutes shall not be followed.
